### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63e47feeca6350f72e77bb05d5475a9a76ac8728` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f9dff246360f8c13538b70503ac69709c6431e8b` — the merge of head `560f410d60af2820a28af588d1dad44b22f2f1b7` into base `63e47feeca6350f72e77bb05d5475a9a76ac8728`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f9dff246360f8c13538b70503ac69709c6431e8b && git checkout f9dff246360f8c13538b70503ac69709c6431e8b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 63e47feeca6350f72e77bb05d5475a9a76ac8728 560f410d60af2820a28af588d1dad44b22f2f1b7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 63e47feeca6350f72e77bb05d5475a9a76ac8728 && git merge --no-ff 560f410d60af2820a28af588d1dad44b22f2f1b7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63e47feeca6350f72e77bb05d5475a9a76ac8728
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 63e47feeca6350f72e77bb05d5475a9a76ac8728` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0cfd82cad07d1a53b32ecbd15d1459b6a3eb582a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-slots-per-package.test.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (`flowNameResolver`, `servedCaller`), packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/plugin.ts (the hook door), .changeset/33748-trigger-disabled-holder.md (declaration lines only)

### ① Derived judgments

- No published schema, export, error code or REST shape moves; `isDisabledHolderSlot` and `disabledHolderDispatchSaid` are private. Right.
- One observable answer moves: a slot of a name two packages hold, whose package is disabled, ran on its trigger on `main` and does not at this head (no run, no run-history row, no substitute). Narrowing only; nothing widens. Right, as amendment 3 of ruling 6884403301 words it.
- `activateFlowTrigger` holds the only `trigger.start` call and wraps `triggerRun`, so every trigger family passes the gate; no trigger plugin needed a change. Right.
- The gate asks the one resolver twice (own holding, then `not-found` on `servedCaller`, which `plugin.ts` answers only under `isPackageDisabled`). A name the registry no longer holds is not judged disabled. Right.
- Amendment 7 holds: the gate returns before `executeKey` and touches no slot key, binding or `flowDispatchHolder`; the runtime pins assert it.
- Check-runs at read time: 28 success, 16 skipped, 6 in progress (Test Core 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 of 8). Nothing red; the Test Core verdict is not yet given.

### ② Semver level

`patch` is the right level (`Metadata-protocol: none`, a non-protocol change). The declaration is wrong.

M1 (must-fix) — `Clause-②: no` with no arm must read `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, on the PR body and the changeset, with `!` in the title and the changeset summary, a `**BREAKING**` banner, exactly one ADR-0087 marker in the changeset body, and the full dogfood battery pinned to the final head. Reasons:
1. The tree takes a behaviour away from a deployed consumer: a trigger-fired run that `main` executes is dropped. AGENTS.md step 3 gives the arm one meaning, direction, and reads `(narrowing)` as BREAKING; "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition".
2. The claim itself says "Narrowing only" and asks for the narrowing review. `contract-review.md` owes that face to a line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the PR body and changeset; a bare `no` owes no ④.
3. "It makes a declared refusal real" settles `no` over `yes`, and settles ④. It does not remove the arm. The refusal was declared by a seat ruling on 2026-11-14; no published text on `main` told a consumer this trigger would stop (ADR-0150 D3 has no disable clause, the docs say nothing on trigger dispatch under a disable). The `execution-duties.md` exemption for a refusal the published text already denies runs in the widening direction only, and needs the quotation.
4. Precedent in this family is uniform: #33646 (same amendment 3; its changeset names this behaviour as its deferred remainder) shipped `yes (narrowing)` with `!`, banner and marker; #32354, #32814 and #32907 shipped `no (narrowing)` with `!`. Card #33748 expected the arm.
`yes` is not owed: no accept-set or public surface widens. The ADR-0087 category is the gate's call; #33646 held `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` for the same reason (no key, row or slot key moves).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, Clause-② copied without the arm: answered by M1. The claim line was wrong; the dev was right to flag it.
- Open question, a name ONE package holds, disabled at runtime, still dispatches: out of this card's scope. Amendment 3 names the slot key `PACKAGE/NAME`, which only a shared name has, and #33646 left single-holder answers "as before". Gating it is a second, wider narrowing over every single-holder package and moves the bare doors with it (amendment 9: doors and engine entries move together). It needs its own card and a seat or maintainer ruling. This PR must not fix it.
- Finding, the served holder of a shared name stays unarmed after a boot disable, and is re-keyed to the bare name and not re-armed after a re-sync `withdrawFlowSlot`: out of scope; the diff touches neither `FlowSlotTable.add/remove` nor `activateFlowTrigger`, and does not worsen it. Not re-measured (read-only). If it holds, it breaks amendment 7 ("a disable moves no key") and silently stops a served package's automation, so the follow-up card is owed now at high priority (silent loss), and it must add the served half to the boot pins. This PR must not fix it.
- Inbound hook: the queued run of a disabled holder's slot is skipped by the same gate (the consumer calls the armed callback). What the door answers the sender is not moved. Read: `inboundHookSlot` admits by `packagedFlowOwner`, with no served check, so a qualified post to a disabled holder's slot is probably accepted and then never run. That is an admission answer (amendments 2 and 8), not a dispatch; follow-up card with a measurement. This PR need not fix it.
- The report's other deviations: accepted, no contract effect.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing is sound. No published text declares that a disabled package's trigger dispatches, so no declared capability is narrowed at the consumer; the ruling's own refusal becomes real. Asked at fire time, it is reversible with no re-arm and moves no key. Tried to break it: an environment slot of a shared name is not gated, correct; an absent or throwing resolver answers "not disabled"; no armed slot reaches `executeKey` around the gate. An event fired during a disable is dropped, not replayed (a one-shot schedule or time-relative fire is lost); that matches "no dispatch" and a switched-off flow.

- N1 (nit) — the boot-disable pins stay green with the gate removed (the dev's ablation A1) and pass while nothing at all is armed, so they pin `main`'s non-arming, not this change. Carrier: the follow-up card of the unarmed served holder.
- N2 (nit) — the changeset does not say that events fired during the disable are dropped and not replayed on enable. Prose face; fold into the M1 rewrite.

M1 is open on this head. Its fix moves the head (changeset, title, battery): a delta review is owed.
